gloss: thank you for your work; good job; goodbye (to colleagues)

definitions.gloss: thank you for your hard work; good job (said to colleagues or coworkers)
definitions.explanation: A standard workplace greeting used to acknowledge someone's effort. Said when meeting colleagues during work, when someone finishes a task, or as a farewell at the end of the workday.

definitions.gloss: goodbye; see you (casual farewell among acquaintances)
definitions.explanation: Used casually as a parting greeting, especially among people who have been doing something together.

examples.english: Thank you for your work. / Good job.

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}も{一日|いちにち}お{疲|つか}れさまでした。
examples.english: Thank you for your hard work today.

examples.japanese: {会議|かいぎ}が{終|お}わると、みんな「お{疲|つか}れさまでした」と{言|い}って{席|せき}を{立|た}った。
examples.english: When the meeting ended, everyone said 'good work' and stood up from their seats.

examples.japanese: {練習|れんしゅう}が{終|お}わって、「お{疲|つか}れ！」と{声|こえ}をかけ{合|あ}った。
examples.english: When practice ended, we called out 'good work!' to each other.

examples.japanese: バイト{先|さき}の{先輩|せんぱい}に「お{疲|つか}れさまです」と{挨拶|あいさつ}した。
examples.english: I greeted my senior at my part-time job with 'otsukaresama desu.'

notes:
One of the most important and frequently used expressions in Japanese workplace culture. It has no direct English equivalent — it functions simultaneously as a greeting, a farewell, and an acknowledgment of shared effort.

FORMALITY LEVELS:
- お{疲|つか}れさまです: standard polite (used with colleagues, seniors)
- お{疲|つか}れさまでした: past tense, used at end of day or after completing work
- お{疲|つか}れ: casual (used among close colleagues, friends)
- お{疲|つか}れさまでございます: very formal (used with superiors or clients)

USAGE:
Used when arriving at work, leaving work, passing colleagues in hallways, after meetings, and as a general acknowledgment. It is considered rude NOT to say it in workplace settings.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ご{苦労|くろう}さま: good work — used by superiors to subordinates; considered rude if used to a superior
- お{先|さき}に{失礼|しつれい}します: excuse me for leaving first — said when leaving before others
